result:
Solutions 1 and 2 give the same answer, p^n + p − 1, which follows from the three orders p−1, p^{n−1}, and p^{n−1}(p−1). I could not fully verify that these are exactly the three qualifying subgroups, since that depends on the classification in the source paper. Their structure is plausible: the full group, the p-Sylow subgroup, and the order-(p−1) subgroup of multiplicative roots of unity are the natural candidates. Solution 3's classification rests on index conditions it does not justify, and it is not a standard characterization, so I reject it.

VERDICT 1: ACCEPT
VERDICT 2: ACCEPT
VERDICT 3: REJECT
